experiment_name: First PROMOTION/generalization gate for the 80-game PURE PPO champion (candidate_ppo_80.pt): candidate focus seat vs three frozen opponent families (032/030/031's 32-game, 64-game, and 128-game checkpoints) on fresh PROMOTION seeds, testing whether it generalizes beyond the single 32-game predecessor it was selected against in 031

algorithm_config.purpose: The 80-game champion (031) was selected purely against the 32-game predecessor. This gate tests generalization against 3 different frozen opponent strengths (32/64/128-game checkpoints, all produced by 031) on held-out PROMOTION seeds never used by any prior run, to check whether the 80-game champion's edge is real strength or an artifact of the single opponent it was tuned against.
algorithm_config.algorithm_frozen: PPOAgent, ActorNetwork/architecture, PPO hyperparameters, reward shaping, action space, state pipeline, evaluation_protocol.py's statistics, and the reference submodule were all unmodified - reuses 028/030/031's exact play_one_game/summarize wholesale (scripts/monopolyzero_pure_ppo_strength_screen.py), no new evaluation framework.
algorithm_config.design: For each of 20 fresh PROMOTION seeds (50000-50019, evaluation_protocol.SEED_CLASS_PROMOTION, verified via require_seed_scope before running): one champion_80 focus seat + three copies of ONE opponent family, rotated across all 4 physical seats = 4 games/seed/family. Three opponent families (A: 32-game, B: 64-game, C: 128-game) x 20 seeds x 4 rotations = 240 physical games total, max_rounds=200, deterministic legal-masked argmax for every seat.

pre_registered_decision_rule.primary_statistic: aggregate candidate win rate across the three equally-weighted opponent families vs. the symmetric 25% null, via evaluation_protocol.seed_block_bootstrap_vs_null with the PROMOTION seed (not seat, not opponent family) as the resampling block - each seed block pools all 12 games (4 rotations x 3 families) sharing that seed
pre_registered_decision_rule.PROMOTION_GO: aggregate 95% CI lower bound for (candidate_win_rate - 25%) is > 0 AND no individual opponent family has a 95% CI upper bound <= 0
pre_registered_decision_rule.note: Per-family win rate/CI is also reported and was pre-registered as diagnostic-cross-check evidence (the second GO condition), never as a standalone override of the aggregate statistic. Behavior metrics (BUY/ACCEPT/DECLINE rates) are diagnostic only, never used in the GO/KILL decision.

result: PROMOTION_GO per the pre-registered rule: aggregate seed-block bootstrap 95% CI for (candidate_win_rate - 25%) = [+13.75, +26.67] points, entirely above zero, AND no individual opponent family's CI upper bound is <= 0 (worst case, family C vs. the 128-game opponent, upper bound is +18.75). Aggregate: 109/240 = 45.42% win rate. Per-family: A (vs. 32-game) 42/80 = 52.5%, GO (CI [+12.5, +41.25]pts); B (vs. 64-game) 41/80 = 51.25%, GO (CI [+15.0, +38.75]pts); C (vs. 128-game) 26/80 = 32.5%, INCONCLUSIVE (CI [-2.5, +18.75]pts, straddles zero). The champion clearly generalizes against the 32-game and 64-game opponent families it was NOT selected against, which is this gate's central question. The aggregate statistic is GO because it pools all three equally-weighted families as one 20-seed-block resampling unit and is not reducible to any single family - it does NOT mean the 80-game champion conclusively beats the 128-game checkpoint individually: family C's own CI straddles zero (INCONCLUSIVE), so no individual-family strength claim vs. the 128-game opponent specifically is supported by this run. 0 illegal actions, 0 crashes, 0 ASU modules loaded across all 240 games.
